comparison: Both evaluate the core POST-IT system design and novelty (C1, C18-C22). OpenEval focuses on technical design rationale and orthogonality, while peer reviewers emphasize the system's innovation and utility for the field. Both find the system well-supported. Peer review also includes in vitro validation claims (C23-C26) and summary claims (C91-C92) that OpenEval evaluates separately.

OpenEval R2 addresses in vitro validation (C23-C26) as foundational experiments, while peer R1 groups these with the overall system design. Both support the findings, with peer reviewers noting the system's utility without questioning the in vitro data.

Both address polypupylation resolution through mutagenesis (C27-C32). OpenEval provides detailed technical validation, while peer reviewers acknowledge 'extensive optimization to enhance specificity and efficiency' after initial concerns about justification were addressed in revision. Both ultimately support the optimization strategy.

Both evaluate PafA optimization to reduce self-pupylation (C33-C35, C47-C48). OpenEval provides detailed assessment of mass spectrometry and mutation effects, while peer reviewers implicitly accept the optimization as part of the successful system development, noting concerns were 'fully addressed' after revision.

Both address in vitro validation with dasatinib (C36-C43). OpenEval emphasizes proximity-dependent labeling and N-terminal HaloTag positioning, while peer reviewers focus on successful target identification and system specificity. Both strongly support these foundational validation experiments.

Perfect overlap on rapamycin validation in live cells (C44-C46). OpenEval details the proximity-dependent mechanism and insight into PafA function, while peer reviewers accept this as part of system optimization without specific concerns. Both support the findings.

Both address final POST-IT optimization including linker length and combined mutations (C49-C50, C99). OpenEval emphasizes additive effects and justification for the final system, while peer reviewers initially raised concerns about experimental design justification but confirmed these were 'fully addressed' after revision. Both support the optimization.

Both evaluate POST-IT functionality in live cells with endogenous targets (C51-C52). OpenEval emphasizes dose-dependent labeling and competitive inhibition as evidence for specificity, while peer reviewers note successful target identification. Both support the findings, though peer R3 focuses more broadly on the overall validation.

Perfect overlap on PafA species comparison (C53-C54). OpenEval notes the differential functionality of Cglu vs Mtb PafA and suggests orthogonality interpretation could be explored further, while peer reviewers accept the characterization without concerns. Both support the findings.

Strong overlap on dasatinib-HTL linker optimization (C55-C58, C96-C97). OpenEval details the literature-guided design and experimental validation of carbamate linkers, while peer reviewers initially questioned the 'random' use of ligand variants but accepted the justification after revision. Both support the optimization.

Perfect overlap on identification of known dasatinib targets (C2, C59-C60, C98). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers strongly support this result as validating POST-IT's target identification capability. Peer reviewers explicitly state the study 'successfully identifies known targets' with 'compelling evidence.'

Perfect overlap on SEPHS2 discovery as novel dasatinib target (C3, C61-C65). Both strongly support the finding with OpenEval emphasizing the low micromolar Kd and docking analysis, while peer reviewers highlight this as an 'important finding' advancing understanding of dasatinib mechanisms. Complete agreement.

Both address POST-IT application to hydroxychloroquine derivatives (C66-C67, C100). OpenEval emphasizes SILAC-based mass spectrometry and autophagy inhibition data, while peer reviewers accept this as demonstrating system versatility. Both support the findings.

Perfect overlap on MST validation of autophagy-related proteins (C68-C70). OpenEval notes appropriate acknowledgment of aggregation issues and differential binding patterns, while peer reviewers accept these as secondary findings with 'compelling evidence.' Both support the results.

Strong overlap on VPS37C discovery as novel HCQ target (C4, C71-C74). Both strongly support this finding with OpenEval emphasizing nanomolar affinity and multiple orthogonal validation methods, while peer reviewers highlight this as an 'important finding' with 'compelling evidence.' Complete agreement on this major discovery.

Strong overlap on zebrafish in vivo application (C5, C75-C77, C89). Both strongly support this result with OpenEval noting lack of toxicity and successful SRC enrichment, while peer reviewers explicitly state this 'demonstrates POST-IT's potential for widespread use' and appreciate toxicity validation experiments. Complete agreement.

Strong overlap on acknowledged limitations (C87-C88, C90). Both accept these as appropriate author-acknowledged constraints. OpenEval notes this is suitable for a methods paper, while peer reviewers indicate initial concerns about data description were addressed in revision. Both support the limitations discussion.

Both address overall POST-IT contribution and summary (C91-C92). OpenEval emphasizes non-diffusive labeling and comparison to TurboID, while peer reviewers focus on novelty and innovation. Both strongly support POST-IT as a valuable contribution, though peer review groups this with system design while OpenEval treats it as a separate summary evaluation.

OpenEval evaluates biological context for SEPHS2 (C80-C82) as supported background information from prior literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as peer reviewers focused on the novel discovery rather than separately evaluating the background context.

OpenEval evaluates mechanistic context for HCQ/CQ and ESCRT complexes (C83-C86) as supported background from prior literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as peer reviewers did not separately assess background information but focused on novel findings.

OpenEval rates mechanistic hypotheses about VPS37C (C101-C103) as UNCERTAIN due to speculative nature and lack of direct experimental validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers did not separately assess these speculative mechanisms, focusing instead on the validated discovery of VPS37C binding.
